title: A geothermal amoeba sets a new upper temperature limit for eukaryotes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed every file in the Figshare collection 8546250 (13 items, CC BY 4.0). Downloaded and opened allTms.csv (64,523 rows: species, gene id, protein sequence, Tm; 22,397 + 21,562 Incendiamoeba proteins from two assemblies, 20,564 Vermamoeba vermiformis; Tm range 32.3-83.1, mean 49.5), results_pilot3_w_KO_PFAM_TPMs.csv (36,543 rows but only 19,717 unique gene ids; DESeq2 output for 48 vs 61 °C, 4 replicates each; log2 fold change range -0.51 to +0.59; 16,093 rows with adjusted p < 0.05, 0 with log2 fold change > 1), sample_metadata.csv (8 samples), incendi_doublingtimes.csv (23 rows), Incendi_Vverm_proteinpredictions.csv (84 rows), analysis_results.csv (32 rows). BioProject PRJNA1329177 exists in NCBI.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Full text was not retrievable (Europe PMC returned HTTP 500); only the abstract was read. That Tm in allTms.csv comes from a sequence-based predictor is inferred from the file (a continuous value for every one of 64,523 predicted proteins, with no proteomics data in the deposit), not confirmed in the methods. Large files not opened: ESM-2 embeddings (1.66 GB), AlphaFold structures (515 MB), ortholog image grids (258 MB).

a1_downloadable.note: Figshare collection, public, CC BY 4.0; files downloaded without login (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Tm (melting temperature) and log2 fold change are both columns in the files (checked), but see A8 and A5.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are inline in allTms.csv and the BRAKER .faa files (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Tm is in °C by context; log2 fold change is unitless (checked headers).

a5_enough_rows.note: The only measured biological label is a single heat contrast: 8 RNA-seq samples (4 at 48 °C, 4 at 61 °C) in one organism. Gene rows (19,717) are not independent experiments, and fold changes are tiny (max 0.59, none above 1).

a6_fits_laptop.note: Tables are small; embeddings tarball is 1.66 GB but optional.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not compare: full text unavailable. RNA-seq table has 36,543 rows for 19,717 unique genes, so rows are duplicated (likely one row per annotation).

a8_label_provenance.note: The only large label (Tm for 64,523 proteins) appears to be a computational prediction from sequence, since every predicted protein has one and no melting experiment is deposited. Training on it would just copy another model.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (embeddings already deposited by the authors)

integration.join_key: none: these are new amoeba gene models with no UniProt accessions
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Would measured melting temperatures of thermophile proteins show the same positive-surface-charge pattern as the predicted ones? This data can't test that, because it holds no measured melting temperatures.

controls.positive_control: none usable: the Tm label is predicted
controls.negative_control: label shuffle would be runnable but meaningless with a predicted label
controls.external_validation: Meltome Atlas could validate a Tm model, but the amoeba proteins themselves have no measured Tm

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here would only reproduce a sequence-based Tm (melting temperature) predictor's output for one amoeba versus one mesophile, or rank genes by a weak 48-vs-61 °C expression shift measured in 8 samples.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use amoeba protein sequences to predict protein melting temperature or which genes switch on when the amoeba is heated.
plain_idea.train_on: Protein sequences from two Incendiamoeba genome assemblies and one ordinary amoeba (64,523 proteins, verified).
plain_idea.predict: Either a melting temperature, which looks like another program's prediction rather than a measurement, or a gene's expression change between 48 and 61 °C, measured by RNA sequencing of 4 versus 4 cultures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could show which protein features let a eukaryote survive above 60 °C, but neither label is a strong enough measurement to support that claim.

label_elsewhere.sources: Meltome Atlas and FireProtDB hold measured protein melting temperatures (known resources); not joinable to this data.
label_elsewhere.join_key: none (no UniProt accessions for these new gene models)
label_elsewhere.why: A real Tm model should be trained on Meltome itself, which makes this paper's predicted Tm values redundant.

ml_idea: Considered: (1) predict per-protein Tm from ESM-2 embeddings, which fails A8 because Tm seems predicted; (2) predict heat-responsive genes from sequence, which fails A5 because it rests on one 4-vs-4 contrast with fold changes under 0.6 log2 units.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes; nothing was timed. ESM-2 embeddings already exist in the 1.66 GB deposit.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Confirm in the methods which tool produced the Tm column. Already effectively done: no melting experiment is deposited.

verdict_reason: The deposit is clean, open and well organised, but its only large label (Tm for 64,523 proteins) appears to be a model's prediction, which fails A8. The one measured label is a single 48-vs-61 °C RNA-seq contrast (8 samples, all fold changes below 0.6 log2 units), which fails A5.
